Nemyriv Old Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Vinnytsia Oblast, Ukraine

Not demolished. This is the older of two Jewish cemeteries in Nemyriv, Vinnytsia Oblast — a different town from the separately documented Nemyriv Jewish Cemetery in Lviv Oblast elsewhere in this collection, which shares the same name. Nemyriv's Jewish community suffered catastrophically during the Khmelnytsky uprising, with 6,000 killed on a single day, June 20, 1648 — one of the largest specific death tolls recorded for that event in this collection. The town was also home to many followers of Breslov Hasidism in the early 19th century, tied to the movement centered at nearby Bratslav, documented elsewhere in this collection. About 3,460 Jews were killed here during WWII, most of them local residents.
